title: Generic Heap: Kth Largest
hints: A heap keeps the smallest (or largest) element on top in O(log n).
Store a comparator closure; sift up on insert and sift down on pop. Keep a min-heap of size k.
`heap.insert(n); if heap.count > k { _ = heap.popTop() }` — the answer is `heap.peek!`.
jsBridge: Swift's standard library has **no heap** (swift-collections has `Heap`), and neither does JS. A generic `Heap<Element>` storing a comparator closure works for min- and max-heaps alike.

compass.q: Neither JS nor the Swift standard library ship a heap. Why might that be?
Stored comparator closure vs `Element: Comparable` + a min/max flag: which is more flexible?
